  "summary": "This three-page English circular, issued by the Hindustani Movement in Bombay in January–February 1977, mobilises citizens for the approaching elections. The movement presents itself as non-political: members may work for and vote for any party or candidate, while the organisation itself does not contest elections. Its central appeal is for Indians to overcome fear, participate actively in democracy, and work with courage, patriotism, dignity, and restraint.\n\nThe circular introduces the “Bhay-Hatao-Dal” (“Remove Fear Group”), a volunteer network whose members pledge to work without financial remuneration, devote fixed time to election work, avoid violence, and support candidates or parties on principled grounds. The accompanying pledge asks members to cast off fear, persuade others to vote, report electoral malpractices, follow candidates’ instructions faithfully, and encourage joint meetings among candidates. A brief covering letter asks recipients to sign and circulate the pledge and related appeal.",
